description:
About the Position

Leiden University advertises a combined lecturer-PhD candidate (docent-promovendus) position in German language and culture. The appointment runs for five years and combines 75 percent doctoral research with 25 percent teaching within the German language and culture programme of Leiden's Faculty of Humanities. The salary follows the Dutch CAO-NU scales for this combined profile, between EUR 3,706 and EUR 4,422 gross per month, and the position leads to a completed doctorate alongside structured teaching experience in a European-studies environment.

The doctoral project sits within Leiden's research on German-language literatures, cultures and linguistics, and the teaching component covers German language instruction and content courses at bachelor's level. The successful candidate receives supervision from the Leiden University Centre for the Arts in Society and its language-teaching units, and follows the faculty's PhD training programme. Because instruction is delivered in German and Dutch academic contexts, near-native German proficiency is required and Dutch is desirable.

Candidate Profile and Application

Applicants hold a research master's degree in German studies, modern languages, linguistics or a related humanities discipline, with an excellent academic record and a clear research interest compatible with the department's profile. Teaching experience is an advantage. Applications - CV, transcripts, research proposal sketch, teaching statement and references - are submitted through the Leiden University careers portal, and the closing date is 8 November 2026.

Highlights

  • 5-year combined lecturer-PhD (docent-promovendus) position
  • 75% doctoral research, 25% German teaching
  • EUR 3,706 - 4,422 gross per month
  • Leiden Faculty of Humanities research environment
  • Near-native German required; Dutch desirable
  • Closing date: 8 November 2026

About Leiden University

Leiden University, founded in 1575, is the oldest university in the Netherlands and a member of the League of European Research Universities (LERU). Its seven faculties in Leiden and The Hague cover humanities, law, social and behavioural sciences, medicine, science, archaeology and governance. Doctoral candidates at Leiden are salaried employees under the CAO-NU collective agreement rather than fee-paying students, which makes its PhD positions fully funded by design. All academic vacancies, including PhD and postdoctoral roles, are advertised on the university's dedicated careers portal.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official page before the deadline: 8 November 2026. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents - early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.
